_comment: Identical to lighthouserc.json except the is-crawlable audit is skipped (W91). A Vercel preview's robots.txt is face-aware and answers Disallow: / (e2e/helpers/face.ts, src/app/robots.ts), which the is-crawlable audit would fail — dragging categories:seo below 1.0 for a reason that has nothing to do with this page's own SEO markup. Skipping the audit removes it from the SEO category's score instead of loosening the assertion; every other SEO check (meta description, viewport, canonical, etc.) still has to score 1.0. `robots-txt` is skipped for the same reason — Lighthouse fetches robots.txt with its own request, which cannot carry the bypass header, so on a protected preview it parses Vercel's login page (W140). gate.sh (and js-size --routes) pass this file to lhci collect AND lhci assert whenever the target wears the preview face — a *.vercel.app host, staging.jobsadmire.com, or NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_FACE set to anything but production (lighthouseConfigFor, e2e/helpers/face.ts; W135/W137): skipAudits is a collect-time setting, so a config handed to assert alone never skips the audit. Production runs (after WP7a) use lighthouserc.json with the audit live. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md § Quality gate. W145 (closes W141): LCP and performance are measured under DevTools throttling (collect.settings.throttlingMethod "devtools"), three runs per path (collect.numberOfRuns), asserted on the median of the three (assert.aggregationMethod "median"). Lighthouse's default simulated throttling (Lantern) charges the whole initial waterfall (framework ~121 KB + next-intl ~17 KB + two Archivo files ~68 KB + CSS) to a text LCP element that has no resource of its own, so a placeholder page read ~2.9-3.0 s while its observed paint under real throttling is ~1.55 s; the LCP and performance assertions keep their values and now judge a real, throttled paint.
